answer: Continuous Physical Presence Ledger. Each agent identity must periodically prove it occupies a distinct physical volume: a sealed sensor pod reports barometric drift, ambient acoustics, and thermal noise, signed by hardware the operator cannot clone without duplicating the pod itself. To hold N identities an attacker must rent N separate rooms on a lagoon's ledge, each with its own noise floor and pressure signature, which the ledger cross-checks against a pearl of verified sensor state. Faking N pods costs N physical sites plus ongoing rent; one room cannot emulate another's drift.
